ai.guide.validator.title: Running a 6529 validator too?
ai.guide.validator.body: Use a separate computer if you can. On one computer, an attacker who exploits a flaw in a model's engine can reach the validator's keys, and a busy model can slow its votes. If you run both, say so when the installer asks: 6529 AI then runs below normal priority.

ai.models.howToRead.today: **Runs in the app today**: its engine is llama.cpp, whisper.cpp or stable-diffusion.cpp, and the app serves what it makes: chat, embeddings, images or speech to text. The other models wait for engines and routes the app doesn't have yet.
ai.models.howToRead.memory: **Memory** is the app's own estimate: the files' size divided by 0.85. A model fits when its files take at most 85% of the GPU's memory, or of the memory a Mac shares with its GPU, and the rest holds the context. A longer context needs more, and the engine has the last word. Without a GPU, the app suggests chat models of up to 5.5 GB, and they run slowly.
ai.models.howToRead.scores: **Scores** are the publisher's own, from its model card at the pinned version, each linked. A percent is rounded to one decimal; a score out of a fixed maximum says so ("8.5 /10"); any other is shown as its card gives it. **†** marks the original model's score: a quantized or changed version can score differently. Cards use different settings, so don't rank models by them.
ai.models.howToRead.measured: **Measured by 6529 AI** marks the runs 6529 timed itself, with the machine and the day.
